input_format: raw HPACK header-block bytes; harness wraps them in valid HEADERS/CONTINUATION frames
configuration_profile: direct real nginx HPACK header-block state machine with a fresh connection pool and dynamic table per input; no HTTP request or routing pipeline
allocator_mode: nginx pools scoped to one parser invocation
justification: NGX-IF10 covers Huffman/integer primitives and NGX-IF11 covers frame headers, but neither decodes HPACK blocks or exercises dynamic-table state and CONTINUATION sequencing.
state: Each block is decoded in one HEADERS frame and with 1-byte, 3-byte, and input-selected frame payload splits. Every run gets a fresh nginx connection and HPACK table.
known_limitations: The hook starts at ngx_http_v2_state_header_block; the initial HEADERS frame header is constructed by the harness and ngx_http_v2_state_headers is not in scope.
The stream is NULL, so decoded fields update HPACK state but bypass HTTP header validation, pseudo-header semantics, request construction, and routing.
The harness emits well-formed CONTINUATION frame headers with the matching stream ID; malformed frame sequencing and network-read fragmentation remain outside this target.
The fuzz-only connection-error guard captures protocol errors without running nginx output/finalization side effects; production parser code otherwise remains unchanged.

scopes.contract: Decode a bounded HPACK block across HEADERS and CONTINUATION payloads, update/retrieve dynamic entries, and stop cleanly on malformed or truncated blocks.
scopes.preconditions: An odd nonzero stream ID, fresh connection/state pools, zero initial dynamic-table entries, valid frame envelopes, and a 65536-byte decoded-header budget.

scopes.contract: Maintain nginx's bounded HPACK dynamic table, including insertion, lookup, resizing, and eviction.
scopes.preconditions: A fresh connection pool; table storage is initialized by nginx on the first incremental-indexing literal.
